summary: CCC steel tower and log cabin on Welch Ridge, Great Smoky Mountains NP, built 1935-36; tower removed (date disputed); cabin remains in poor condition.

facts.design: Steel tower, 46 feet, with a log cabin (chestnut-shake roof, stone chimney)
facts.status_note: Tower removed, date disputed (late 1980s or early 1990s); a crumbling log cabin remains near the tower footprint. One Pigeon Forge page says the tower remains.

access.note: Inside Great Smoky Mountains National Park; reached on foot by backcountry trails

visit.trail_note: Nothing to climb. SummitPost describes the most direct route as beginning at Lakeview Drive and going through a tunnel.

events.note: Civilian Conservation Corps built the steel tower and log cabin from 1935 to 1936; a crew of seventeen men was sent in October 1935

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The story treats the tower as removed, which the Mountain Press body text, SummitPost and the Smoky Mountain News essay all support. The Mountain Press introduction and a Pigeon Forge page suggest it still stands; the story names both views rather than dropping them.
The 2010 Smoky Mountain News essay gives the late 1980s; a 2016 Citizen-Times column, as SummitPost reports it, gives the early 1990s. The story reports both and does not pick one.

notes_for_editor: The Mountain Press article is internally inconsistent: its introduction lists High Rocks among standing towers, while its High Rocks section says the tower has been removed. The 2016 Asheville Citizen-Times column was not read directly; it is cited only as SummitPost reports it. The LOC photo listing returned 403, so the HABS photographs were not seen; only the record's title and location were read. Elevation differs: Mountain Press gives 5,185 feet for the cabin, SummitPost gives 5,190 feet for the peak; the story gives no elevation. The Smoky Mountain News and SummitPost pieces are personal or community writing, so their dates are used only as attributed claims. The record's status is unknown; the research supports marking it gone with the cabin remaining.
